_comment: Method parameters. 'default' applies to every dataset; a dataset's own block (its data-file name without _quantification) wins and may override single parameters. Unset parameters keep the method's own default. These 'default' values are best-judgement settings aimed at the best achievable score per method (longer training, no early stopping that cuts training short, over-clustering for the clustering methods). They have NOT been tuned on your data: run `python cli.py tune` to refine them per dataset. List every parameter with `python cli.py params`; validate this file with `python cli.py params --check`.

_notes.xgboost: 1000 trees max with early stopping on the validation split (30 rounds), learning rate 0.1, depth 8, row/column subsampling 0.8 (the old default stopped at 100 trees).
_notes.random_forest: 500 trees, balanced class weights (criterion is fixed to log_loss by the repo wrapper and is slow).
_notes.logistic_regression: max_iter 2000 (the default 100 usually does not converge on standardised markers), C 10, balanced class weights.
_notes.svm: RBF with C 10 up to 50k training cells; above that it falls back to LinearSVC (an RBF SVC on more cells is too slow).
_notes.louvain: resolution 1.5 and 15 neighbours: over-clustering helps because clusters are greedily mapped to labels afterwards.
_notes.spade: 50 clusters (more than the cell types) and 10k down-sampled cells.
_notes.singler: uses every marker (n_top larger than the marker count).
_notes.scanvi: scvi's own defaults (50 epochs, 1 layer, 128 hidden, 10 latent, batch 128): the old run trained cleanly with them (0.67) and the loss had flattened by epoch 20. A bigger network (2 layers, 256 hidden, 30 latent, batch 512) diverged to NaN at the first batch.
_notes.scarches: scvi defaults, 50 reference epochs and 20 query epochs, same network as scanvi.
_notes.spatial_gnn: 15 spatial neighbours, 2 hops, less regularised logistic regression (C 10, 1000 iterations).
_notes.leiden: five resolutions up to 5.0 (more clusters than cell types score better after greedy mapping); 15 neighbours.
_notes.tacit: r 200 and p 20 = the TACIT authors' own settings for this CRC dataset (runTACIT_paper.R); the package default r 10 gives far too few micro-clusters. Leiden n.iter = 2 is hard-coded in the authors' function too, so it matches their runs.
_notes.scyan: preprocess=true standardises every marker first (Scyan's prior expects that; it was missing before), up to 200 epochs with min_delta 0.1 (Scyan's default min_delta 1 stops very early), up to 500k cells per epoch (default 200k).
_notes.astir: 100 epochs, 10 initialisations, tighter convergence, assignment_type=max so cells are never left 'Unknown' (the default 0.7 threshold turns uncertain cells into Unknown, which counts as wrong).
_notes.tribus: outlier_quantile 1.0 keeps all cells (the wrapper dropped cells above the 99.9th percentile), library-default clustering_threshold 15000 instead of 100, tuning=10 lets Tribus fit sigma and learning rate, other_threshold 0.2 so fewer cells become 'other'. Its 500 SOM iterations are hard-coded in the package.
_notes.starling: up to 200 epochs with early-stopping patience 20 (the wrapper's Lightning default of 3 stopped training almost immediately), 30 initial clusters.
_notes.maps: 300 epochs (min 50, patience 50) instead of the hard-coded 2, batch 256, standard_split=true so MAPS trains on the 80% training fold (the original script trains on the 20% fold and predicts the other 80%).
_notes.stellar: 100 epochs, 256 hidden units, graph radius 3x the median neighbour distance.
